newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel rebuffs pleas it ease up on PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel rebuffs pleas it ease up on PLO.

text.p: Israel on Monday kept up its pressure on the Palestinian Authority to fight militants despite pleas it ease punitive measures imposed after bloody Jerusalem suicide bombings.

"We cannot really understand some measures that instead of bringing security are bringing insecurity," Miguel Angel Moratinos, the European Union's Middle East envoy, said at a Gaza news conference with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Moratinos also failed to persuade Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to lift tough measures imposed on Palestinians after two Arab suicide bombers killed 13 people and wounded 170 in a West Jerusalem market on Wednesday.

"Envoy Moratinos...brought a Palestinian request to ease the pressure on the Palestinan Authority and the steps Israel has taken against it," Netanyahu's office said in a statement issued after he met Moratinos on Monday afternoon.

"The prime minister told Moratinos that Israel was acting against terror and not against the Palestinian people...and that Israel was taking different steps in order to pressure the Palestinian Authority to fulfil its obligations."

After Wednesday's bombings, Israel suspended peace talks with the PLO and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, disrupting Palestinian trade preventing tens of thousands of Arab workers from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state.
It also threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to fight militants if Arafat did not do the job. Israel has arrested 145 suspected militants in areas under its control.

Under interim peace deals between Israel and the PLO since September 1993, Israel remains in charge of international borders. The Palestinian Authority is in charge of self-rule enclaves set up in most of Gaza and parts of the West Bank under the deals.
Israel's Treasury said it had frozen the transfer of $70 million in tax revenues it owes the PLO.
"Israel is at this stage delaying funds to the Palestinian Authority until it meets its obligation...to fight terror," a statement quoted Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman as saying.
Palestinians have said the Israeli measures are collective punishment and that they weaken Arafat.
The Palestinian Health Ministry said in a statement that Israel's closure was causing widespread medical problems.

It said Palestinian medical personnel and supplies were unable to reach hospitals, pregnant village women were unable to reach city hospitals and that patients requiring urgent treatment in Israel or Arab states were in danger.
Veteran U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross is expected to visit the region later this week to tackle the months-long peace crisis that was only deepened by Wednesday's attack.
Earlier, Netanyahu had said the Authority had to decide to be "a regime that fights terrorism like Jordan and Egypt, or a regime that encourages terrorism like Iraq and Iran".
He made the comment before talks with U.S. Republican Senator Phil Gramm, a staunch supporter of Israel. Gramm said Congress might not renew aid to the Palestinian Authority.

"Authorisation for Palestinian aid, as you know, expires on August 12. It will not be renewed by the United States Congress in my opinion unless the Palestinians begin living up to the commitments they've made," Gramm said.

Palestinians, who suspended security cooperation with Israel after Netanyahu launched a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, say they have nonetheless worked to foil attacks by militants opposed to the peace process.
A leaflet issued in the name of the Islamist Hamas group claimed responsibility for Wednesday's attack, but Israeli and Palestinian officials say they are not sure of its authenticity.

Arafat was to meet King Hussein later on Monday in Amman. Jordanian officials privately expressed their support of Arafat's view that the bombings were being exploited by Israel to backtrack on peace commitments.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, who goes to Egypt for talks with President Hosni Mubarak on the crisis on Tuesday, said Israel "doesn't want the collapse of the Authority" but that it had to fight militants.

Israel on Monday demolished three illegally built homes in Arab East Jerusalem. Palestinians say demolitions are aimed at squeezing them out of the city. Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and vows never to cede an inch of it. Palestinians want it as capital of a future state.

In south Lebanon, the last active Israeli-Arab front, Israeli commandos raided suspected pro-Iranian Hizbollah targets. Hizbollah said five guerrillas were killed by roadside bombs after the clashes. Five civilians were wounded.
